disclaimer: Educational research prototype only. Not validated for clinical use. This result is not a medical diagnosis.

sections.title: Dataset provenance
body: Breast Cancer Wisconsin (Diagnostic): 569 samples, 30 real-valued features, binary label (malignant / benign). Created by Dr William H. Wolberg, W. Nick Street and Olvi L. Mangasarian (University of Wisconsin); donated to UCI in November 1995; licensed CC BY 4.0.

Features were computed from digitised images of fine-needle aspirates (FNA) of breast masses. An operator outlined cell nuclei with an interactive 'snake' contour tool; ten nuclear characteristics were measured and their mean, standard error and 'worst' (mean of the three largest) values recorded per image [street1993].
The dataset contains no images, no mammograms and no patient demographics. Loaded via scikit-learn, which mirrors the UCI copy [sklearn_ds].

sections.title: Preprocessing and leakage control
body: No missing values or duplicate rows exist; nothing is imputed. Sample IDs are not used as features (the scikit-learn copy does not include them).
Labels re-encoded so 1 = malignant (positive class). scikit-learn's native encoding is the reverse (0 = malignant).
Stratified hold-out split: 455 training / 114 test (seed 42). The test split is not used for tuning, selection, calibration, threshold choice or EDA statistics.
Standardisation is fitted inside scikit-learn Pipelines, i.e. on training folds only. Tree models and Naive Bayes are not scaled.

sections.title: Algorithms
body: Logistic Regression, SVM (RBF, Platt-calibrated), Random Forest, Decision Tree, K-Nearest Neighbours, Gaussian Naive Bayes and (optional) Gradient Boosting, each with a small hyperparameter grid suitable for an 8 GB laptop.
No deep learning: with 455 training rows of tabular features, conventional models are appropriate and easier to audit.

sections.title: Evaluation methodology
body: Nested cross-validation (RepeatedStratifiedKFold(5 x 2) outer, StratifiedKFold(5) inner grid search on ROC-AUC) on the training split gives approximately unbiased performance estimates for selection [varma2006].

Selection rule: max nested-CV ROC-AUC; within-1-SE pool -> min CV Brier; then simplicity. Highest nested-CV ROC-AUC: Logistic Regression (0.9950 ± 0.0019 SE). Candidates within one standard error of that value (Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (RBF)) were treated as statistically indistinguishable; among them the one with the lowest mean CV Brier score (best probability quality) was chosen, with model simplicity as the final tie-break. Selected: Support Vector Machine (RBF) (CV ROC-AUC 0.9948, CV Brier 0.0214, CV recall 0.9500). The held-out test set was not used.
Calibration: Apply sigmoid calibration only if it lowers out-of-fold training Brier by > 0.002. Applied: none.
Operating threshold: 0.39 — Largest threshold in [0.05, 0.5] whose out-of-fold training recall >= 0.97 (5-fold CV on the training split only).

The selected model was then evaluated once on the untouched test split; percentile bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (1000 resamples) accompany test metrics. Test results for non-selected models are shown for transparency only.

sections.title: Explainability
body: Global: permutation importance (drop in test ROC-AUC), standardised coefficients or impurity importance where native, mean |SHAP|, and feature correlations.

Local: SHAP permutation explainer on P(malignant) with a 50-row training background [shap]. Attributions describe model behaviour, not biology; correlated features (radius/perimeter/area) share credit unpredictably.

sections.title: Reporting and regulatory context
body: Documentation follows the spirit of TRIPOD+AI [tripod_ai] where applicable (data source, predictors, outcome, sample size, missing data, model development, performance, limitations). This is a development study only: no external validation exists.

Software that analyses medical images or signals, or provides patient-specific diagnostic output, may fall under device regulation [fda_cds]. OncoSense is an educational prototype and must not be used for clinical decisions.
